trust_decision.summary: Whether a vCenter connection verifies the server certificate is decided by a hardcoded boolean at every client-construction site, not by any request field: inspector, forecaster (two separate clients), rightsizing and the collector's forklift Secret all pass skip-verify=on, so all six credential-bearing HTTP routes reach vCenter with certificate verification disabled.

landing_point.why: The shared govmomi client constructor every handler-driven connection goes through; its 'insecure' parameter is documented as 'use only for testing' (pkg/vmware/client.go:21) yet both production callers pass a literal true (internal/services/inspector.go:97, internal/services/forecaster.go:114). An engineer reading only the summary lands here or on those two call sites.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/rightsizing/vsphere.go:66-87 with the hardcoded Insecure:true at internal/services/rightsizing.go:252-258

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The rightsizing stack is a completely separate govmomi client (its own Config.Insecure knob at pkg/rightsizing/vsphere.go:39-44) and the caller carries a written justification that skipping verification is an accepted risk for self-signed on-prem vCenter (internal/services/rightsizing.go:252-257), so a solver can call it deliberate configurable behaviour rather than the hardcoded bug in the report.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Backwards compatibility: a request that supplies neither cacert nor skipTls must still connect with verification skipped, and skipTls=false with no cacert must stay legal. Every existing client and the whole e2e suite POST only url/username/password against a self-signed vcsim and expect 202, so defaulting to verification (or rejecting skipTls=false/absent) breaks them; the same default feeds the automatic rightsizing run triggered from POST /collector.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: test/e2e/service/agent.go:175-180 and internal/services/rightsizing.go:466-481 (auto-trigger uses the collector's credentials verbatim)

O6_input_shapes: flat credential object body (POST /collector, PUT /forecaster/credentials, POST /inspector/credentials)
cacert as a PEM string, possibly a multi-certificate bundle (x509.CertPool.AppendCertsFromPEM)
skipTls as a tri-state pointer bool: absent / true / false
cacert together with skipTls=true must be rejected with 400
cacert that contains no parseable PEM must be rejected with 400
skipTls absent + cacert present means verify with that CA; skipTls absent + no cacert keeps skip-verify for compatibility

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This very fix added cacert/skipTls to the v2 spec and generated type, yet no v2 handler exists (only apiV1 is registered, cmd/run.go:130-133), so the next maintainer to wire v2 writes its own mapping

O8b_injection_room.sibling: persist cacert/skipTls through Encrypt/Decrypt and a widened credentials table so a saved credential reconnects with the same TLS mode
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Credential encryption plus master-password storage is the immediately preceding commit (ECOPROJECT-4648), models.Credentials was just given json tags for the new fields, and the round trip silently drops them

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a route that starts a run from the cached savedCreds without ever calling Credentials.Validate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The forecaster already carries an in-memory credential cache reused by POST /forecaster when no body credentials are sent

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second credential source for the automatic post-collection rightsizing run that does not inherit the collector's TLS fields
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: POST /api/v1/collector silently starts a rightsizing collection with the collector's credentials, so any new producer of those credentials is a new route into pkg/rightsizing without the report naming it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second Kubernetes Secret builder for a different collector/validator backend that again writes insecureSkipVerify
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: TLS for the forklift collector is expressed purely as Secret keys, so every new consumer of provider credentials needs its own key set
